name: Views entity_access check
description: Runs $entity->access('view') on every row a configured view returns during hook_views_pre_render(), dropping rows the current user may not see.
project_description:
TL;DR: Adds a "view" ($value->_entity->access('view')) access check on each views row pre-render. Try this module if you're using a custom access restriction module but entities keep showing up in views which the users can't access and should not be shown. Only enable on views where needed, until core issue #777578 is solved.

Why and when is this helpful? Drupal's Entity Access API provides a great toolkit to define access for entities. Still, hook_entity_access() has a weak point: it is not called for listings (e.g. from entity queries and Views). For nodes, the additional grant system (since Drupal 6) is used instead, so nodes are even more special. As it's not possible to provide an SQL-based solution for all permission modules (which calculate permissions at runtime with complex logic in hook_entity_access), these modules won't work as expected in Drupal Views (and EntityQueries). Typically you'll see entities listed in views which the user can not access ("Access Denied") and in the worst case it means information disclosure. There's a core issue to find better ways: #777578, but until this is solved this module provides a hacky workaround implementing hook_views_pre_render() and checking "view" access on the _entity property.

Affected access / permission modules include entity_access_by_reference_field, entity_access_by_role_field, and Access by Reference, which can't implement hook_query_TAG_alter() and handle non-node entities.

Notes & Downsides: this should be seen as a quickfix. Access checking each entity in the view decreases performance and thereby should only be used in views where it's needed. Whenever possible hook_query_TAG_alter() should be implemented in access modules. This may have further downsides, so test carefully, especially in combination with caching and complex access restrictions. This module will probably never have a stable 1.0.0 release, hopefully core will provide a nice DX solution instead.

Installation & configuration: identify the views where you have the described issues, install the module, go to /admin/config/system/views-entity-access-check and select only the views to run the additional access check on, then check if your issue is gone and test carefully.

Similar modules: Views Entity Operation Access provides an access plugin for the view to hide it entirely based on an entity permission. Maintained by DROWL.
